# Section 4.2: Enhanced Lane Change Decision Making

⚠️ **WARNING:** Autopilot is a hands-on driver assistance feature that does not make the vehicle autonomous. You must keep your hands on the steering wheel at all times, maintain control and responsibility for your vehicle, and be prepared to take immediate action at any time. Failure to follow these instructions could cause damage, serious injury or death.

Autopilot's lane change feature assists the driver in changing lanes on the highway. When the feature is active, the vehicle can identify appropriate gaps and execute lane changes, while the driver remains responsible for monitoring the driving environment and maintaining control of the vehicle at all times. This section describes how the system evaluates lane change decisions and the safety parameters that govern this behavior.

The system uses Tesla Vision—8 cameras providing 360° coverage—combining wide, main, and narrow forward views with side and rear cameras for comprehensive situational awareness. A vision-based occupancy network models the surrounding free space and nearby vehicles in real time.

When initiating a lane change, the vehicle will:

• Monitor the adjacent lane for 2.5 to 6 seconds before initiating
• Calculate optimal merge timing based on relative vehicle speeds
• Engage turn signals automatically when safe to proceed
• Abort the maneuver if unsafe conditions are detected (see Section 4.2.1)

The system only initiates a lane change when there is sufficient space in the target lane. The required gap increases automatically at higher speeds and when surrounding vehicles are moving at significantly different speeds.

A lane change requires a minimum confidence level before the maneuver begins. This threshold is automatically raised in higher-complexity environments, as shown below.

## Confidence Thresholds

| Driving Context | Confidence Threshold |
|-----------------|----------------------|
| Base (default) | 90% |
| Highway (good visibility) | 92% |
| City Streets* | 94% |

*City streets functionality requires FSD Beta enrollment

Knowing when and why the system may cancel a lane change helps you anticipate the vehicle's behavior and stay ready to take over.

## Section 4.2.1: Lane Change Abort Conditions

⚠️ Never depend on Navigate on Autopilot to determine an appropriate lane change. Always check your blind spots, mirrors, and signal before changing lanes.

The system continuously evaluates merge safety throughout a lane change and will abort the maneuver if any of the following conditions are detected:

• Lane change confidence drops below the required threshold
• A new vehicle enters the target lane
• An adjacent vehicle accelerates toward the vehicle's path
• The gap in the target lane closes faster than is safe to merge
• You provide steering input or manually cancel the turn signal
• A system fault is detected

When a lane change is aborted, the vehicle smoothly returns to the original lane and resumes lane keeping. You will be notified by an audible chime and a "Lane Change Cancelled" message on the display, which remains visible for approximately 3 seconds. Steering assistance transitions back gradually to maintain a smooth, predictable feel.

⚠️ Driver supervision required. You must be prepared to take over immediately at any time.
